title: ARCHITECTURAL DESIGN CHARACTERISTICS, USES, AND PERCEPTIONS OF COMMUNITY SPACES IN PERMANENT SUPPORTIVE HOUSING

findings.antecedent: Presence of community spaces in facility
findings.mechanism: Community spaces provide opportunities for social interaction and support, contributing to well-being.
findings.quote: Stressed the importance of having community spaces in the facility

findings.antecedent: Presence of community spaces in facility
findings.mechanism: Staff recognize the role of community spaces in supporting residents' well-being and recovery.
findings.quote: Stressed the importance of having community spaces in the facility

findings.antecedent: Gathering spaces
findings.mechanism: Gathering spaces provide opportunities for residents to interact and build relationships.
findings.quote: Reported that gathering spaces support formation of community

findings.antecedent: Gathering spaces
findings.mechanism: Staff observe that gathering spaces facilitate resident interaction and community building.
findings.quote: Reported that gathering spaces support formation of community

findings.antecedent: Community spaces
findings.consequent: Social development of residents exiting homelessness (perceived by residents)
findings.mechanism: Community spaces offer a context for residents to practice social skills and reintegrate.
findings.quote: Reported that community spaces support social development of residents exiting homelessness

findings.antecedent: Community spaces
findings.consequent: Social development of residents exiting homelessness (perceived by staff)
findings.mechanism: Staff observe that community spaces aid in the social development of residents.
findings.quote: Reported that community spaces support social development of residents exiting homelessness

findings.antecedent: Community lounge space in Booth Centre
findings.mechanism: Factors like location, visibility, and policy likely impede use.
findings.quote: None of the Booth Centre participants reported using the lounge space in their building.

findings.antecedent: Community spaces in Westgate
findings.mechanism: Easier accessibility and visibility in Westgate likely contribute to higher reported use.
findings.quote: Over 90% of Westgate resident participants use the community spaces regularly, and 86% reported using them twice a week or more.

findings.antecedent: Planned activities in Westgate community spaces
findings.mechanism: Low attendance suggests planned activities may not fully meet resident needs or overcome barriers to participation.
findings.quote: only 6% of participants reported attending such events during their residence.

findings.antecedent: Deeper location of community space in building
findings.mechanism: Increased spatial steps and reduced visibility make spaces harder to locate and reach.
findings.quote: The deeper the community space located in the building, the more difficult it will be to find and access.

findings.antecedent: Additional effort required to locate community space
findings.mechanism: Higher cognitive load or physical effort acts as a barrier to use.
findings.quote: Any additional effort required of the resident to locate the space reduces the likelihood that it will be used

findings.antecedent: Location and easy visual/physical access of community spaces
findings.mechanism: Easy access and visibility reduce barriers to entry and allow for assessment of social situations.
findings.quote: location and easy visual and physical access was the most important characteristic of community spaces

findings.antecedent: Lack of visibility of community spaces
findings.mechanism: People prefer to assess a space from a safe distance before entering; lack of visibility prevents this.
findings.quote: data support the notion that visibility, or lack of it, is a key reason that community spaces may be underused.

findings.antecedent: Ability to see and assess who is in a space from a safe distance
findings.consequent: Comfort in making space use decisions
findings.mechanism: Allows individuals to manage social interaction and perceived safety.
findings.quote: People feel more comfortable making space use decisions when they can see and assess from a safe distance who is in the space

findings.antecedent: Walking into a space without ability to evaluate from safe psychological distance
findings.consequent: Vulnerable position for residents with history of stress/violence
findings.mechanism: Lack of control over social exposure and potential threats increases feelings of vulnerability.
findings.quote: Walking into the space without the ability to evaluate from a safe psychological distance puts a person in a vulnerable position.

findings.antecedent: Need to make a 'prospect and refuge' decision on the spot
findings.mechanism: The immediate pressure to decide on entry without prior assessment leads to avoidance.
findings.quote: Knowing that one would need to make a 'prospect and refuge' decision on the spot may lead residents to avoid approaching the space.

findings.antecedent: Incorporation of distinct functional zoning (e.g., wider pathways, low partitions, plants, high-back furniture)
findings.consequent: Sense of privacy in each area
findings.mechanism: Physical separation and visual barriers create perceived private zones within a larger space.
findings.quote: Incorporation of distinct functional zoning separated by wider pathways, low partitions, plants, or furniture with higher backs may create a sense of privacy in each area sufficient to encourage residents to increase their use

findings.antecedent: Adjacency of community spaces to kitchens
findings.mechanism: Residents view cooking/eating and recreational activities as separate functions.
findings.quote: adjacency of community spaces to kitchens was not important for residents at either site

findings.antecedent: Residents cooking in community kitchens
findings.mechanism: Lack of cooking skills or habit among formerly homeless individuals.
findings.quote: very few residents who cooked in the community kitchens.

findings.antecedent: Residents cooking/warming up meals in community kitchen
findings.mechanism: Desire for privacy during meals, even after using communal cooking facilities.
findings.quote: even if residents cook or warm up their meal in a community kitchen, they prefer eating in the privacy of their own rooms.

findings.antecedent: Aesthetic factors (cleanliness, acoustics, lighting quality, personalization, hominess)
findings.consequent: Residents' sensory and mental perceptions of community spaces
findings.mechanism: These qualities contribute to a sense of comfort, dignity, and belonging.
findings.quote: This group of factors affects residents' sensory and mental perceptions of community spaces

findings.antecedent: Actual and perceived cleanliness of supportive housing
findings.consequent: Sense of dignity and self-esteem for residents
findings.mechanism: Cleanliness counters stigmatization associated with homelessness and fosters a sense of personal worth.
findings.quote: Research suggests that actual and perceived cleanliness affects the sense of dignity and self-esteem

findings.antecedent: Noise from loud conversations and TV in Booth Centre community spaces
findings.consequent: Issue for residents whose rooms were adjacent
findings.mechanism: Lack of acoustic privacy between community spaces and private rooms causes disturbance.
findings.quote: noise from loud conversations and TV was an issue for the Booth Centre residents whose rooms were adjacent to the community spaces.

findings.antecedent: Westgate community spaces not sharing partitions with living room
findings.consequent: Overall positive assessment of community space
findings.mechanism: Improved acoustic privacy contributes to a more positive perception of the space.
findings.quote: Westgate community spaces, in contrast, do not have rooms that share partitions with the living room, which contributed to the overall positive assessment of the community space.

findings.antecedent: Larger windows allowing more natural light into rooms
findings.mechanism: Natural light is associated with positive feelings and well-being.
findings.quote: participants pointed out that windows could be larger to allow more natural light into the rooms.

findings.antecedent: Presence of blinds on windows (Westgate)
findings.mechanism: Blinds contribute to a sense of privacy and control, enhancing feelings of hominess.
findings.quote: One Westgate resident noted how pleasant it was to have blinds on the windows, associating that with feelings of home.

findings.antecedent: Personalization (unique art, decorative objects, clocks, furniture, accessories) in community spaces
findings.consequent: Emotional investment and sense of ownership
findings.mechanism: Personal touches make a space feel more individual and cared for.
findings.quote: Personalization is crucial to emotionally investing in a place and creating a sense of ownership

findings.antecedent: Scarcity of furnishings in Booth Centre cluster lounges
findings.mechanism: Lack of comfortable, varied furnishings contributes to a sterile, impersonal environment.
findings.quote: two residents at the Booth Centre noted that the scarcity of furnishings led to an overpoweringly institutional feeling

findings.antecedent: Institutional policy restricting access to community spaces (only residents of cluster/house or invited guests)
findings.consequent: Residents feeling restricted in recreational and socialization choices
findings.mechanism: Policies intended for security inadvertently limit opportunities for broader social interaction.
findings.quote: policy of restricting access to residents... but the study's findings suggest it makes residents feel restricted in their recreational and socialization choices.

findings.antecedent: Opportunity to socialize around an activity or event
findings.consequent: Perception of caring gesture by residents
findings.mechanism: Organized social opportunities convey support and value to residents.
findings.quote: when residents... have an opportunity to socialize around an activity or an event, they perceive it as a caring gesture.

findings.antecedent: Booth Centre 2nd floor spatial configuration
findings.mechanism: The physical layout dictates the extent of visible space from various points.
findings.quote: Isovist area % of Floor Area = 24.6%

findings.antecedent: Booth Centre 2nd floor spatial configuration
findings.mechanism: The layout's depth and connectivity determine its overall visual integration.
findings.quote: Mean integration = 4.1

findings.antecedent: Booth Centre 2nd floor spatial configuration
findings.mechanism: Low SD indicates enclosed and poorly visually integrated spaces.
findings.quote: Integration SD = 0.82

findings.antecedent: Westgate boarding house spatial configuration
findings.mechanism: The physical layout dictates the extent of visible space from various points.
findings.quote: Isovist area % of Floor Area = 35.6%

findings.antecedent: Westgate boarding house spatial configuration
findings.mechanism: The layout's depth and connectivity determine its overall visual integration.
findings.quote: Mean integration = 7.7

findings.antecedent: Westgate boarding house spatial configuration
findings.mechanism: Higher SD indicates spaces with low and high visual integration.
findings.quote: Integration SD = 3.1

findings.antecedent: Higher mean integration of spaces
findings.consequent: Higher level of visibility in a configuration
findings.mechanism: Integration measures how connected a space is to all others, directly correlating with visibility.
findings.quote: The higher the mean, the more integrated the spaces are, suggesting higher level of visibility in a configuration.

findings.antecedent: Lower integration SD in a configuration (e.g., Booth Centre)
findings.consequent: Spaces tend to be enclosed or poorly visually integrated
findings.mechanism: Low SD indicates uniformity in integration, often due to enclosed, less connected layouts.
findings.quote: The majority of spaces in a configuration with a lower integration SD would tend to be either enclosed or open, such as the Booth Centre, where spaces are enclosed and poorly visually integrated.

findings.antecedent: Higher integration SD in a configuration (e.g., Westgate)
findings.consequent: Spaces with low and high visual integration
findings.mechanism: High SD indicates a greater variety in how integrated spaces are, suggesting a mix of open and more secluded areas.
findings.quote: The configuration containing spaces with low and high visual integration will have higher SD, such as the Westgate's boarding house.

findings.antecedent: Booth Centre spatial layout (partitioned/enclosed spaces)
findings.consequent: Users' opportunities to assess community spaces
findings.mechanism: Physical barriers and lack of visual integration prevent users from seeing into spaces.
findings.quote: users experience greatly reduced opportunities to assess the community spaces available to them.

findings.antecedent: Not knowing if anyone is using community space (due to lack of visibility)
findings.consequent: Disincentive to look for and visit community space (for socially anxious persons)
findings.mechanism: Social anxiety is exacerbated by uncertainty about social encounters, leading to avoidance.
findings.quote: not knowing if anyone is using the community space further disincentivizes looking for and visiting the community space

findings.antecedent: Confusing wayfinding within Booth Centre (signage, colors, design features)
findings.mechanism: Inconsistent visual cues and lack of clear navigation paths make it difficult to orient oneself.
findings.quote: wayfinding within the Centre is confusing, with signage, colors, and design features being almost indistinguishable on different floors.

findings.antecedent: Westgate community space (visible right away from multiple vantage points on first floor)
findings.consequent: Users quickly know how many others are in the space and who they are
findings.mechanism: High visual integration allows for rapid assessment of social conditions.
findings.quote: This greater visibility quickly tells users how many others are in the space and who they are.

findings.antecedent: Visual accessibility organized along central axes, static/predictable sightlines
findings.consequent: Overall sense of control and institutionality of configuration
findings.mechanism: Predictable and controlled visual paths can contribute to a less personal, more institutional feel.
findings.quote: visual accessibility is organized along the buildings' central axes. Spaces are linked longitudinally, and sightlines remain for the most part static and predictable, adding to the overall sense of control and institutionality of the configuration.

limitations: Accessing and working directly with persons who had experienced homelessness was a challenge.

Participants may have believed that the facility administration was aware of their participation, potentially affecting their responses (e.g., prompting more complimentary answers about facilities' designs and policies).
A number of resident participants spoke in dry, institutionalized language of personal responsibility and asserted gratitude for being in the facility.

The questionnaire sample size presents a limitation for generalizing the findings derived from its data alone; the study's overall goal was to explore a phenomenon, not to produce empirically verifiable results generalizable to a broader population.

The study did not address any background characteristics of the respondents, such as personal histories, relationships, health, or where they were in the process of exiting homelessness with regard to residents.
The study did not address the hierarchy of organization, experience with working with homeless persons, or position (i.e., case worker or management) with regard to staff.
